item: A Stop is not a market feed's failure in the scheduler's markets pass or the import-all route: the feed it cut and the ones after it are neither checked nor failed, and the route says how many were not asked (R377)
summary: import_due_feeds and POST /api/markets/feeds/import-all ran every feed through import_feed and counted anything not imported as failed. import_feed already files a failure under an engaged switch as the offline verdict (R320), but both callers then counted that verdict as the feed's failure and walked every later feed through a refusal too, so one Stop became N failures in the scheduler tally and N offline results in the route response. Both callers now read the switch at the top of each iteration and the offline verdict (and an exception with the switch engaged) after the check, and end the pass: the cut feed and the unasked ones are neither checked nor failed; the route adds skipped_offline (present only then, the verify_due_feeds idiom) with the count not asked. Host answers keep their own verdict (robots, an HTTP status: a Stop cuts connections and cannot produce a status line) and stay failures. Stated limit: a genuine failure coinciding with a Stop reads as the Stop (R320). The Load / Refresh / Retry verdict box draws the count with the key the law tracker already uses ("{n} not fetched (airplane mode)", already x12), because the cut feeds are no longer offline failures in results and a partial load would read as complete (found by the read). Not changed: the single-feed routes (one verdict, already honest) and monitoring/field_test.py (opt-in). Red-before as run: 7 of 9 tests fail on the old code, the two ordinary-failure controls pass on both.
